interpretation: Checkpoint-mean binary log loss for membership anywhere in the next authoritative batch, not full-action cross-entropy or true conditional entropy
limitations: At most three preselected candidates; panel coverage is reported separately
Partition labels alone do not verify fresh held-out tasks or a preregistered freeze
Missing predictions remain declared failures without invented probabilities
Paired loss differences use jointly scored checkpoints only
Task success, physical execution work and prediction hit rate are separate outcomes
Three-candidate top-3 hit rate measures panel coverage, not ranking improvement
Timing is prediction replay wall time, not live task latency
Failures before dispatch retain their denominator but have no fabricated compiled prompt

definitions.binaryLoss: Original C8 -log(max(1e-12, recorded score for the actual binary membership)); mean over panel candidates, then checkpoints.
definitions.falsePositiveFalseNegative: Exploratory orientation of the recorded binary score around0.5; ties are separate. This is not a changed runtime admission threshold or a calibrated decision rule.
definitions.highConfidenceDiagnostic: Continuous wrong-label score summaries and counts at the existing loss floor; no new high-confidence cutoff or recalibration.
definitions.lossConcentration: Candidate losses weighted by inverse panel size before shares, preserving the original checkpoint-mean objective.
definitions.familyDifference: Mean paired checkpoint difference within each original development family; each contributes one-sixth to the existing paired estimate.
definitions.Top1: Highest recorded score using unchanged exact-identity tie break, evaluated over all52 eligible read checkpoints with missing predictions retained as misses.

limitations: Post hoc explanation on development data only; this diagnostic is not an additional hypothesis test or preregistered finding.
Recorded raw scores are autoregressive binary conditionals, not verified independent marginal probabilities.
Failed predictions retain their original denominators and receive no invented probability or loss. The jointly scored subset is reported separately.
No raw task, tool arguments, candidate identity, checkpoint text, or private annotation is emitted.
No model call, recalibration, changed threshold, new confidence interval, held-out access, or scientific configuration change.
